name: Eve
notes: Genesis gives no age for Eve.

name: Shem
notes: Born two years before Noah was 500? Genesis 5:32 groups the three sons at Noah’s 500th year; Genesis 11:10 says Shem was 100 two years after the flood (AM 1656), which gives AM 1558.

name: Sarai
notes: Ten years younger than Abraham (Genesis 17:17); died at 127 (Genesis 23:1).

name: Abraham
notes: Genesis 11:26 lists Abram first among Terah’s sons at Terah’s 70th year, but Genesis 11:32, 12:4 and Acts 7:4 together imply Abram was born when Terah was 130. Years from here on use that reading and are therefore estimates.

name: Esau
notes: Twin of Jacob (Genesis 25:24-26). No death age is given.

name: Joseph
notes: Jacob entered Egypt at 130 (Genesis 47:9) when Joseph was about 39 (30 at his appointment, Genesis 41:46, plus seven years of plenty and two of famine, Genesis 45:6). Joseph died at 110 (Genesis 50:26).

name: Moses
notes: Israel entered Egypt about AM 2298; Exodus 12:40 gives 430 years in Egypt (Exodus 12:40), and Moses was 80 at the Exodus (Exodus 7:7) and died at 120 (Deuteronomy 34:7). Galatians 3:17 counts the 430 years from the promise to Abraham instead, which would move these dates by about two centuries.

name: Ram
notes: Luke 3:33 reads “Admin, the son of Arni” where Ruth 4:19 and Matthew 1:3-4 have Ram.

name: Heli
notes: Named as Joseph’s father in Luke 3:23; Matthew 1:16 names Jacob. Explanations offered since Julius Africanus (3rd c.) include levirate marriage or adoption.

name: Mary
notes: Luke 3:23 calls Joseph the son of Heli. The idea that Heli was actually Mary’s father (making Luke’s list her line) is a traditional harmonization, not something the text states, so no father is drawn here.

name: Jesus
notes: Born before Herod the Great died in spring 4 BC (Matthew 2:1-19); most scholars place the birth c. 6–4 BC. The year is an estimate.

name: Rahab
notes: Mother of Boaz according to Matthew 1:5; the Old Testament does not record the marriage.

name: Uzziah (Azariah)
notes: Matthew 1:8 jumps from Joram to Uzziah, omitting Ahaziah, Joash and Amaziah (2 Kings 8:24; 12:21; 14:21). Matthew’s three sets of fourteen (1:17) are a deliberate arrangement, not a complete list.

name: Jeconiah (Jehoiachin)
notes: Matthew 1:11 makes Josiah the father of Jeconiah; 2 Kings 24:6 makes Jehoiakim (Josiah’s son) his father. “Father” in Hebrew genealogies can mean ancestor.

name: Joseph (husband of Mary)
notes: Matthew 1:16 names his father Jacob; Luke 3:23 names Heli. Both are drawn.
